newsitem.title: USA: First Union says credit card writeoffs rose.
newsitem.headline: First Union says credit card writeoffs rose.

text.p: First Union Corp's net credit card writeoffs rose in the first quarter to a 7.28 percent rate from 5.75 percent in 1996's fourth quarter, when sales of bad loans improved the writeoff rate, First Union executives said on Thursday.

Chief credit officer Mal Murray said during a telephone call with reporters that credit cards accounted for six percent of the large regional bank's loans and that without the late 1996 loan sales the change in the credit card rate would have only been about 100 basis points.
Murray gave First Union's gross writeoff rate in credit cards for the first quarter as 7.79 percent, up from 6.78 percent during the last three months of 1996.

First Union said in its quarterly earnings report issued earlier that annualized net chargeoffs for all its loans were 0.61 percent in the first quarter, down from 0.66 percent during the first quarter of 1996.
Chief Financial Officer Robert Atwood said First Union expects its fee-based businesses to keep growing strongly into the next century.
Income from fee-based businesses such as managing capital should grow at more than 25 percent a year on a compounded basis over the next five years, Atwood said.
